newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds edged lower on Thursday and dealers said investors were getting somewhat nervous as the gaining dollar versus the German mark and Dutch guilder could trigger a rate hike.
Dealers said the shorter end of the curve had been off for some days but longer dated guilder-bonds also started to dip in afternoon trade.
"It was a volatile session," said one dealer, adding investors started to think that a rate rise might come earlier than expected as result of the gaining dollar.
The yield curve flattened further today, but the yield gap with Germany was stable.
"It is the same story for Dutch bonds as it is for German bunds," said one dealer, explaining both debt markets were closing watching exchange rate movements.
Another dealer said rates in Germany and the Netherlands were likely to come closer to those in other European markets with the Euro emerging.
"This means that rates in the Netherlands are likely to move up as rates in Spain and Italy - for instance - are higher," he said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
